topics.name: Areas of segments and combined figures

questions.title: 16 equal sectors, radius 7 cm: one sector's area
questions.text: A circle is divided into 16 identical sectors. If the radius of the circle is 7 cm, the area of each sector is:
questions.remember: Equal sectors: area of one = πr² ÷ (number of sectors).
questions.trap: Picking 77/4 by dividing by 8 instead of 16.
questions.tryit: A circle of radius 14 cm is cut into 8 equal sectors. Find one sector's area.

questions.title: Arc 11 cm, radius 6.3 cm: find θ
questions.text: Arc PQ subtends an angle θ at the centre of a circle with radius 6.3 cm. If arc PQ = 11 cm, then the value of θ is:
questions.remember: Arc length = θ/360 × 2πr. Work it backwards to find θ.
questions.trap: Using πr² (area) instead of 2πr (circumference) for an arc.
questions.tryit: Arc 22 cm, radius 21 cm. Find θ.

questions.title: Wheel of diameter 21 cm over 66 km: revolutions
questions.text: A car has wheels of diameter 21 cm. The number of complete revolutions each wheel makes in covering a distance of 66 km is:
steps: ① One revolution covers one circumference = πd
questions.remember: Revolutions = distance ÷ circumference (both in the SAME unit).
questions.trap: Dividing 66 km by 66 cm directly and getting 1. Convert km to cm first.
questions.tryit: A wheel of diameter 70 cm makes how many turns in 1.1 km?

questions.title: Arc 6π cm, sector area 24π cm²: radius?
questions.text: The length of an arc of a circle is 6π cm and the area of the corresponding sector is 24π cm². The radius of the circle is:
steps: ① Shortcut: sector area = ½ × r × arc length
questions.remember: Sector area = ½ × r × l (l = arc length). No θ needed!
questions.trap: Trying to find θ first. It works, but it's long. Use the shortcut.
questions.tryit: Arc 10 cm, radius 7 cm. Find the sector's area.

questions.title: Diameter 28 cm, arc 22 cm: sector area
questions.text: Find the area of the sector of a circle of diameter 28 cm, if the length of the corresponding arc is 22 cm.
steps: ② Sector area = ½ × r × l
questions.remember: Sector area = ½ × r × l. Always halve the diameter first.
questions.trap: Using r = 28 (the diameter). That gives double the answer.

questions.title: Chord at 120°, radius 21 mm: perimeter of the segment
questions.text: Chord AB of a circle with centre O and radius 21 mm subtends an angle of 120° at the centre. Find the perimeter of the minor segment (the region between chord AB and arc AB). (Use √3 = 1.73)
steps: ① Perimeter of segment = arc AB + chord AB
③ Draw OM ⊥ AB: it bisects AB and ∠AOB ⟹ ∠AOM = 60°
questions.remember: Perimeter of a segment = arc + chord. Perimeter of a sector = arc + 2 radii.
questions.trap: Finding the AREA. Read again: the question asks for the PERIMETER.
questions.tryit: Radius 14 cm, angle 60°. Find the chord length.
